fluff.overview: The Newgrange class was the largest mobile shipyard ever constructed, with each vessel stretching to nearly double the length of a McKenna-class battleship. Designed by Di Tron Heavy Industries of Terra and introduced in the early twenty-seventh century, these enormous vessels served as the backbone of the SLDF's mobile repair and refit infrastructure. Each Newgrange functioned as a self-sufficient orbital factory capable of traveling between star systems, carrying the personnel, equipment, and raw materials needed to service even the heaviest capital vessels far from any fixed shipyard. Despite their intimidating presence in fleet formations, these vessels carried only modest armament relative to their enormous mass and relied heavily on escort ships for protection against dedicated attacks. Few classes in the history of interstellar warfare have commanded such reverence among naval engineers and fleet commanders, and the loss of even a single vessel was considered a strategic catastrophe.
fluff.capabilities:
Each Newgrange displaced 2,300,000 tons and stretched 2,680 meters from stem to stern, with a 3,000-meter jump sail. The forward unpressurized repair bay alone accounted for 2,100,000 tons of capacity, large enough to enclose and service virtually any WarShip in existence. Onboard manufacturing and assembly facilities could fabricate replacement components as needed, and the cargo bays held sufficient material to house a fully dismantled destroyer. Four 250-meter gravity decks provided comfortable living and recreation facilities for a complement exceeding seven thousand crew, repair technicians, and passengers. A battalion of WorkMeks supported repair operations, while a fleet of small craft facilitated personnel transfers.

Propulsion came from conventional drives delivering a safe thrust of two and maximum of three, supplemented by a standard Kearny-Fuchida drive with an integrity of 44 and four docking collars. Ferro-Carbide armor provided 600 tons of protection across all arcs, backed by a structural integrity of 25. The weapons suite consisted of eight Barracuda missile launchers, eight Naval Laser 45s, eight Naval Laser 55s, sixteen ER Large Lasers, eight PPCs, and forty Anti-Missile Systems. This was respectable for self-defense but inadequate against dedicated naval opposition. Seven hundred eighty-seven double heat sinks managed thermal loads. The standard variant also carried a Mobile Hyperpulse Generator, enabling independent interstellar communication.
fluff.deployment:
The most famous individual Newgrange was the vessel known successively as Blake's Mercy, Mercy, and Clementia. Hidden at the secret Gabriel base in the Odessa system under Word of Blake control, it was deployed to Coventry to repair the stranded Immortal Spirit. Coalition forces captured the massive YardShip during the liberation of Coventry in March 3074, sparking an ownership dispute between the Lyran Commonwealth and Clan Jade Falcon that Devlin Stone ultimately resolved by securing the vessel for the Republic of the Sphere. Sent to Terra to bolster the rebuilding O'Neil Yards, the vessel was renamed Clementia under Republic naval conventions and served alongside sister ships Harmonia and Necessitas until all three were decommissioned and mothballed in the late 3120s. Reactivated by RAF remnants during the ilClan era, the vessel was seized by Clan Snow Raven at Eris in July 3151.

The SLS J. Swift participated in Project AMHITRITE in 2683, transporting a Monitor-class prototype from Mars to New Earth but suffering severe structural and drive core damage during the jump. After five months of repairs, the J. Swift was stationed at Epsilon Pegasus before disappearing in 2755 during an explorer vessel recovery mission. Nearly four centuries later, Clan Snow Raven's Deep Periphery exploration teams recovered the long-lost YardShip, which appeared at Epsilon Eridani in February 3152 alongside two other recovered Star League vessels.
fluff.history:
Di Tron Heavy Industries of Terra introduced the Newgrange class in 2600, creating what would become the definitive mobile shipyard of the Star League era. The first operational vessel salvaged and repaired battle-damaged WarShips from the Reunification War's brutal Battle of Robsart as early as 2603, demonstrating the class's strategic value within just three years of its commissioning. Over the following decades, approximately two hundred Newgranges were constructed, forming the backbone of the SLDF's mobile repair and refit infrastructure. Their ability to service capital vessels in forward operating areas transformed SLDF fleet logistics, allowing damaged WarShips to return to frontline duty without the lengthy transit to fixed shipyards.

In 2776, the SLDF's remaining Newgranges underwent top-secret modifications at the Krester shipyards near Keid in preparation for Operation LIBERATION, the final assault on the Amaris-held Terran system. After the liberation and General Kerensky's Exodus, only about forty-five Newgranges remained in the Inner Sphere. The early Succession Wars proved devastating to these irreplaceable vessels. YardShips were prime targets because they could neither jump nor maneuver while servicing another vessel, and hostile forces recognized that destroying a single Newgrange crippled an enemy's ability to maintain its remaining WarShip fleet. By the thirty-first century, the class was believed extinct.

ComStar reportedly based its smaller Faslane YardShip design on the remains of two derelict Newgrange hulls maintained at hidden shipyards near Terra, while secretly preserving at least one intact vessel at a covert facility. When ComStar fractured, the Word of Blake inherited these hidden assets. The dramatic reappearance of a Newgrange during the Jihad shocked the Inner Sphere, proving the class still existed. The Republic of the Sphere subsequently operated three vessels before mothballing them in the late Republic era. The class experienced an unexpected resurgence in the 3150s when vessels long thought lost were recovered and returned to active service, nearly five centuries after the first Newgrange was launched.
